implementation_summary: Authored src/persistence/raw-event-log-store.ts, the fact/accepted-event half of PersistenceAdapter (appendFact, loadFacts, appendAcceptedEvent, loadAcceptedEvents), as idempotent lookup-before-insert IDB stores over createKVStore (src/marmot/storage.ts). Storage layout is one array value per group key (RawProtocolFact[] under rawFactsKey(groupId), AcceptedDomainEvent[] under acceptedEventsKey(groupId)) rather than one IDB key per item -- this makes both ordering contracts (loadFacts seq-ascending, loadAcceptedEvents append-order) hold by construction (array push order === insertion order === the monotonic append position) and sidesteps the documented idb-keyval keys()-is-key-sorted trap entirely, since there are no per-item keys to enumerate. appendFact is the sole seq authority: a duplicate id returns the existing stored fact with its original seq and duplicate:true, minting no new seq; a fresh id gets (current max seq)+1, scoped per group. appendAcceptedEvent is a strict no-op on a duplicate id (no second entry, no write at all) -- this is the AC-INV-2 persistence-side proof the S3 task-projector formally depends on as a precondition. IDB keys are sourced exclusively from src/engine/engine-types.ts's rawFactsKey/acceptedEventsKey function calls (never inlined literals), satisfying the sanctioned persistence -> engine-types carve-out and AC-BOUND-3. legacy-key-guard.structural.test.ts implements AC-MIG-1's CI gate: a write-call-site-specific scanner (inspects only the first-argument text of setItem(/set( calls, not a blanket occurrence scan) that flags any write to the legacy notestr:events: key outside src/store/persistence.ts, deliberately narrow enough to not false-positive on src/marmot/storage.ts's pre-existing, legitimate migration read/copy code.
test_count_reconciliation_note: Explicit new-file test counts (14 in raw-event-log-store.test.ts + 9 in legacy-key-guard.structural.test.ts = 23) do not fully reconcile the full-suite baseline->final delta (707->733 = +26) on their own -- the residual +3 is the same self-scaling-structural-test effect S3's result.json documented: engine-boundary.structural.test.ts's AC-BOUND-3 suite (a PRE-EXISTING, unmodified suite from S1) recursively scans all of src/ and emits one `it` per file discovered outside engine-types.ts, so it automatically grew by 3 (one per newly created src/persistence/*.ts file) without this story touching that test file. Verified by re-running `npx vitest run` (733/733 green, 33 test files up from 31) both before and after an independent manual flip-proof cycle (see empirical_verification) confirmed no residual state corruption.

judgment_calls: Storage layout is one array per group key (not per-item IDB keys), making both ordering contracts hold by construction rather than by a derived sort. See architecture.json 'single-array-per-group-storage-layout' and verification.json (pre-impl commitment set covers this via VQ-S4-004/007; no post-impl question needed -- the design choice is directly observable in the file and independently confirmed correct by the delete-before-update interleaving test).
seq assignment is O(1) via (last element's seq)+1 rather than an O(n) max-scan, relying on the array being seq-ascending by construction. See architecture.json 'seq-assignment-strategy'.

No in-process concurrency lock on the read-then-write append path -- matches the exact posture of the legacy src/store/persistence.ts:appendEvent this replaces, not a regression, out of this story's explicit scope. See architecture.json 'no-concurrency-lock-matches-precedent'.

AC-MIG-1's scanner is write-call-site-specific (inspects setItem(/set( first-argument text) rather than a blanket key-literal-presence scan (the AC-BOUND-3 style), specifically to avoid false-positiving on src/marmot/storage.ts's pre-existing legitimate migration read/copy code. See architecture.json 'ac-mig-1-scanner-is-write-call-site-specific-not-blanket-presence'.

The scanner also legitimately trips on src/marmot/storage.test.ts (a pre-existing test fixture literal-writing to the legacy key to simulate pre-migration data for a migration-correctness test) -- a genuine ambiguity not anticipated by the story brief, which pre-authorized excluding only persistence.ts. Excluded storage.test.ts alongside persistence.ts with documented reasoning (test-only historical-state simulation, not a new production write path) rather than either silently ignoring the hit or unilaterally rewriting an out-of-scope file. Recorded as verification.json VQ-S4-P1 (post-impl, confidence 0.9) for examiner/future-phase-boundary review rather than treated as settled without a paper trail. See architecture.json 'storage-test-ts-second-exclusion-not-pinned-down-by-story-brief'.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The AC-MIG-1 structural gate's exclusion list needed a second entry (src/marmot/storage.test.ts) that the story brief did not anticipate -- the brief's exclusion clause named only src/store/persistence.ts, but a correctly-written write-call-site scanner (needed anyway to avoid false-positiving on storage.ts's legitimate migration read/copy code) also legitimately catches a pre-existing test fixture in storage.test.ts that literally writes to the legacy key to simulate historical data for a migration test. Diagnosing this required reading storage.test.ts's actual fixture content (not just storage.ts) to distinguish 'a second real violation the AC exists to catch' from 'a pre-existing, sanctioned, test-only historical-data-simulation write that happens to share the scanner's write-call shape' -- a distinction the story brief's text alone did not resolve, since it discusses only production write paths. Resolved via a documented judgment call (excluded, with an explicit load-bearing-exclusion proof test and a post-impl verification question) rather than silently absorbing or blocking on it.
retrospective.surprised_by: The full-suite delta (707->733, +26) did not match the two new test files' own counts (14+9=23) at first glance -- the residual +3 came from engine-boundary.structural.test.ts's pre-existing AC-BOUND-3 suite auto-discovering the 3 new src/persistence/*.ts files via its own recursive src/ scan. This is the identical self-scaling-structural-test effect S3's retrospective already flagged for a different pair of suites (domain-boundary.structural.test.ts / engine-boundary.structural.test.ts against src/domain/) -- worth noting again since it recurred on a different structural test (AC-BOUND-3 this time) against a different new directory (src/persistence/), suggesting any story that adds files under a directory already covered by an existing self-scanning structural test should expect this reconciliation step, not just the two files S3 already called out.

absorbed_from.note: Implemented all four PersistenceAdapter methods exactly per the architect's pre-specified algorithm (no redesign), wrote both test files with full coverage of the mandated scenarios (idempotency, seq monotonicity, per-group seq isolation, delete-before-update interleaving ordering, AC-MIG-1 scanner with liveness fixtures), ran and reverted two flip-proof mutation cycles per file, and explicitly surfaced the storage.test.ts double-exclusion ambiguity rather than silently resolving it -- flagged in its final report and documented in the test file's own module doc comment. No disagreement with its framing; its reasoning for the storage.test.ts exclusion is folded verbatim into this story's architecture.json judgment call and verification.json VQ-S4-P1 above, and independently spot-verified by the architect (re-ran the empirical 'exclusion removed -> violations become exactly [storage.test.ts]' check) before accepting it.
